sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Main menu container and list
sections.what: Creates the outer navigation container and the list that holds the menu entries. It also places the shared viewport under the menu where open panels appear.
sections.why: Likely reason: the viewport must sit inside the root so panels line up under the menu.
sections.watch_out: Removing the viewport from the container stops dropdown panels from showing.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Dropdown trigger, panel and viewport
sections.what: Makes the clickable heading that opens a menu, the panel content that animates in and out, and the viewport that holds the panel. The trigger adds a small arrow that turns when open.
sections.why: Likely reason: the animation and rotating arrow show the user that a menu is open.
sections.watch_out: The animation classes need the animation plugin in the Tailwind setup, which is not visible here, so animations may silently do nothing.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Highlight indicator and export list
sections.what: Creates a small pointed marker that appears under the active heading, then lists all parts for other files to import.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the usual dropdown look.

summary: Provides the building blocks for a top navigation bar whose headings open dropdown panels, styled to match the app.
purpose: Lets a screen build a top menu where hovering or clicking a heading opens a panel of links.
why: Likely reason: it wraps a ready-made navigation library and applies the app's styling so the menu looks consistent.
how: The root container holds a list of items. Each item can have a trigger heading that opens a content panel. A shared viewport at the root shows the open panel and animates it in and out. Links and a small pointed indicator are also provided.
inputs: Child elements placed inside each piece, plus style and layout overrides passed as props.
outputs: Rendered navigation menu components that appear in the page, including dropdown panels when opened.
risks: The dropdown panels depend on the viewport being rendered inside the root; removing it stops panels from showing. The long class strings depend on Tailwind and theme variables that are not visible in this file.
debug: If panels do not open, check that trigger and content sit under the same root and that the viewport is present. If styling looks wrong, check the trigger style helper and any overrides passed by the parent.
